criteria.evidence: Delta 446cbe9e..4c415c21. runId is required and serialized in TailoringNavKey/TailorFailedNavKey; TailorFailedNavigation.retry reuses key.runId; the SPEND carries productId run-<runId> and is recorded after the upsert inside TailoringCreditSpend.forSuccess, so a failure or cancel records nothing and a crash after the result reruns once and spends once (crashAfterResultBeforeSpendRerunsAndSpendsExactlyOnce, retryAfterFailureReusesTheRunAndSpendsAtMostOnce, reTailorOfTheSameApplicationWithANewRunRunsAndSpendsOnceMore). Round-2 finding 1 fixed. Check-then-record is not atomic (credit_ledger has no unique productId), but production wiring yields one runner per runId: the VM key is runId inside the entry's ViewModelStore, Navigator.navigate drops an equal key and replace swaps the Retry key in place, so a double tap on Retry stays one VM. No deep link builds TailoringNavKey; the debug target mints a UUID per open. Open: the fresh UUID defeats navigate()'s equal-key dedupe on a double tap of Tailor (finding 1), and in prod the run-<runId> marker never exists once the ledger is server-owned (finding 2).

TailoredPaperMapper highlights the summary only when its decision is ACCEPTED; restoredProfileSummaryIsNotHighlightedButAcceptedTailoredSummaryIs covers REJECTED and PENDING -> None, ACCEPTED -> FromResume. Round-2 finding 3 fixed.

TailorEntryRealWiringTest renders entryProvider { tailorEntry(navigator) }(TailoredNavKey) from the production provider under a plain ViewModelStoreOwner pre-filled at TailorViewModelKeys.tailor/tailored; hiltViewModel gets no Hilt factory there, so a reverted key = applicationId misses the store and NewInstanceFactory throws. Taps Accept changes and asserts changesAcceptedAt. Round-2 finding 2 fixed.
No I.1/I.2 regression: the delta changes only highlight colour, the spend/marker order and nav keys; the assembler and ExportReadiness are untouched, and nothing unaccepted reaches export.

TailoringCreditSpendTest null -> run-r1 is justified (forSuccess now takes runId and writes the marker) and stronger: it pins the productId. The removed crashBetweenSpendAndResult test covers a state that can no longer occur (SPEND is written after the result). The edits to ShellWalkTest, ScreenChromeTest, TailorEntryKeysTest and TailorFailedNavigationTest only add the runId constructor argument. CI at 4c415c21: Static checks, Constitution policy and pregate pass; Core/Feature/App unit tests, Screenshot tests, Lint and Assemble APKs were pending when reviewed.

findings.rule: 278-c2 one SPEND per user tap; D56 'each tap makes a new runId'; Navigator.navigate drops an equal key (core/navigation Navigator.kt line 14)
findings.trigger: Double tap on Tailor or Re-tailor, or a second tap while the outgoing screen is still composed during the transition. At 446cbe9e both calls built an equal TailoringNavKey(app-1) and Navigator.navigate dropped the second one. Now each call mints a new UUID, so the stack becomes [.., Tailoring(r1), Tailoring(r2)]. r2 runs and spends, then replace() swaps it for Tailored. Back from Tailored composes Tailoring(r1), which runs again: a second SPEND in demo, a second server debit in prod, and the result the user just reviewed is overwritten.
findings.title: A fresh runId per call defeats the navigator's duplicate-key guard, so a double tap charges twice
findings.proof: Test: Navigator(NavigationState(NavBackStack<NavKey>(ApplicationDetailNavKey("app-1")))).apply { navigateToTailoring("app-1"); navigateToTailoring("app-1") }; assert state.stack.filterIsInstance<TailoringNavKey>() has size 1 (fails today: 2). Fix: fun Navigator.navigateToTailoring(applicationId: String) { if ((state.currentKey as? TailoringNavKey)?.applicationId == applicationId) return; navigate(TailoringNavKey(applicationId, UUID.randomUUID().toString())) }

findings.rule: 278-c2 / D56 skip a run whose SPEND exists; #319/#287 prod record() is a no-op and observeLedger() is server-owned (OfflineFirstCreditsRepository.record on origin/revamp/287-billing-v2; RemoteCreditsLedgerSource maps TAILORING with the server's productId, never run-<runId>)
findings.trigger: Prod after #319 merges: the user starts tailoring and backgrounds the app. The activity saves state with TailoringNavKey(app-1, r1). The server finishes, RemoteResumeTailor clears PendingTailoringIds for (app-1, all), and the result is stored. The process is then killed in the background. On restore, TailoringNavKey(app-1, r1) reruns and alreadySpent is false because no run-r1 row exists. PendingTailoringIds mints a new requestId and apps-backend begin() (src/apps/tailormyresume/tailoring.ts ~line 274) calls reserveCredit again, because it is idempotent only per (userId, requestId). One tap is charged twice. D56 assumes the device ledger order matters only for demo, but the device SPEND row is also the skip marker.
findings.title: In prod the run-<runId> skip marker never exists, so a restored run calls the server with a new requestId and is charged again
findings.proof: Fix: pass runId into the tailoring call, through TailorResumeUseCase and ResumeTailor.tailor(..., runId). In RemoteResumeTailor, key PendingTailoringIds by runId instead of applicationId and keep the id after SUCCEEDED (clear it only on a FAILED finish or a non-resumable failure). A rerun of the same runId then resends the same requestId and the server returns the finished job with no debit (be-all test 'a repeated requestId returns 200 with no model call and the total spend stays one credit'). Retry after FAILED still gets a fresh requestId. Test (testProd): MockWebServer; run RemoteResumeTailor twice with the same runId after a SUCCEEDED finish and assert both start requests carry the same requestId. If #317 does not own app/src/prod, file this against #319 before it merges.
